Synthetic crossed and nested data for learning G theory

Source: R/datasets.R
mfrmr_gtheory_data.Rd

Existing tutorial examples supplied as ready-to-load tables. Load one with data("mfrmr_example_gtheory_crossed", package = "mfrmr"), then assign it to a shorter name such as ratings. No simulation code is needed to run the G-study or D-study examples.

Format

Two data frames with five columns: Person, Rater, Task, Content, and Organization. Each row is one Person-by-Rater-by-Task rating cell; the last two columns are continuous numeric scores. mfrmr_example_gtheory_crossed has 1,920 rows (40 Persons, eight common raters and six common tasks). mfrmr_example_gtheory_nested has 540 rows (30 Persons, six tasks and three raters per task).

Source

The existing crossed G-theory tutorial (seed 24) and nested G-study help example (seed 2027). Their unchanged generation recipes are retained in data-raw/make-teaching-data.R in the source repository.

Details

In the crossed example, the same rater ID denotes the same rater on every task. In the nested example, R1, R2, R3 are local labels: the pair Task and Rater identifies a rater, giving 18 raters in total. Declare nesting = c(Rater = "Task") for that example. Persons are crossed with all tasks and rater teams in both examples.

The scores were constructed from independent normal random effects for every source in the respective design. The nested example correlates the two score components within each source. These are fictional unbounded continuous scores, not ordered rubric categories or MFRM ability estimates. Their design and sample sizes demonstrate the functions; they do not establish that an assessment's assumptions or estimation precision are adequate.

See also

mfrm_g_study(), mfrm_d_study(), mfrm_multivariate_d_compare(), load_mfrmr_data()

Examples

data("mfrmr_example_gtheory_crossed", package = "mfrmr")
ratings <- mfrmr_example_gtheory_crossed
head(ratings)
#>   Person Rater Task Organization    Content
#> 1      1     1    1    0.5045747  0.5475769
#> 2      2     1    1    1.3440571 -0.9615514
#> 3      3     1    1   -0.4715306  3.7099968
#> 4      4     1    1   -0.5425612  0.5795908
#> 5      5     1    1   -0.3337672  2.8174334
#> 6      6     1    1    1.6440213  0.1798085
g <- mfrm_g_study(ratings, scores = c("Content", "Organization"),
  person = "Person", rater = "Rater", task = "Task")
g$component_diagnostics
#>         Source MinimumScaledEigenvalue    Tolerance PositiveSemidefinite Rank
#> 1       Person              0.12937911 1.490116e-08                 TRUE    2
#> 2        Rater              0.07993328 1.490116e-08                 TRUE    2

#> 6   Rater:Task              0.14198058 1.490116e-08                 TRUE    2

# Inspect component estimates before projecting future plans.
d <- mfrm_d_study(g,
  design_grid = data.frame(Raters = c(2, 4), Tasks = 3),
  weights = c(Content = .5, Organization = .5))
summary(d)
